leads.title: Papua New Guinea Penal Code - Section 210
leads.documents: Criminal status of male same-sex sexual activity; punishes sodomy/anal or oral sex with up to 14 years imprisonment and other same-sex acts with up to 3 years.
leads.detail: Cited in text as 'Section 210 of the Papua New Guinea Penal Code' with 14-year and 3-year penalties; no URL visible in article text.

leads.title: Government of Papua New Guinea communication to the United Nations (2011)
leads.documents: Official government position that decriminalising homosexuality was not a priority, showing legal reform stance.
leads.detail: Cited as 'In 2011, the Government informed the United Nations that decriminalising homosexuality was not a priority'; no URL visible.

leads.title: United States Department of State reporting on Papua New Guinea (2012)
leads.documents: Enforcement monitoring: no reports of prosecutions directed at LGBTQ persons in 2012, but LGBTQ persons 'vulnerable to societal stigmatization'.
leads.detail: Cited as 'According to the United States Department of State, there were no reports of prosecutions in 2012'; no URL visible.

leads.title: ILGA report on Papua New Guinea
leads.documents: Enforcement incidents: 2015 arrest/conviction for 'indecent acts' between males with suspended sentence, community service and mandatory counseling; 2022 arrest of two men after having sex.
leads.detail: Cited as 'According to an ILGA report, arrests occurred in 2015 and 2022'; no URL or full report title visible.

leads.title: 2011 study cited by ILGA on violence against men who have sex with men and trans people
leads.documents: Rights/enforcement machinery: finds police were one of the main sources of violence against men who have sex with men and trans people.
leads.detail: Cited as 'a study in 2011 which found police were one of the main sources of violence'; authors/title/URL not visible.

leads.title: US Department of State Human Rights Report on Papua New Guinea - 2017
leads.documents: Documented incidents and enforcement abuse: discrimination, gay men in Port Moresby sexually abused by police, raped and beaten, with power imbalance and victims framed as perpetrators.
leads.detail: Cited as 'In 2017 the US Department of State Human Rights Report on Papua New Guinea revealed several incidents'; no URL visible.

leads.title: Statement by Prime Minister Peter O'Neill on homosexuality
leads.documents: Government political stance opposing decriminalization; cites 'strong feelings' against homosexuality and country 'yet to accept such sexual openness'.
leads.detail: Attributed in text to Prime Minister Peter O'Neill in context of Dame Carol Kidu 2012 decriminalisation call; no URL visible.

leads.title: Statement by former MP Dame Carol Kidu (2012)
leads.documents: Political/rights context: gay Papua New Guineans forced to live lives of secrecy; unsuccessful call on Government to decriminalise homosexuality.
leads.detail: Attributed as 'Former MP Dame Carol Kidu in 2012 described... and called unsuccessfully'; no URL visible.

leads.title: Statement by Prime Minister James Marape (2023)
leads.documents: Current government refusal to repeal criminalisation of male homosexuality; claims current laws sufficient to protect against violence/abuse and cites Melanesian and Christian worldviews.
leads.detail: Cited as 2023 confirmation with direct quote beginning 'There is no bill with our government to promote gays and lesbians'; no URL visible.

leads.title: Queensland Criminal Code / Australian-extended criminal law
leads.documents: Legal origin of PNG criminalisation: Australian criminal law derived from Queensland Criminal Code created during British colonization extended to PNG and retained after 1975 independence.
leads.detail: Cited in history discussion of Australia's occupation and 1975 decriminalization divergence; no URL visible.
